title: Quantization Technical Review - Stargazer AI
summary: Deep technical review focused on quantization strategy for Stargazer's chat model. Covered INT8 vs FP8 vs GPTQ/AWQ tradeoffs, accuracy regressions observed in internal tests, KV-cache implications, batching/latency, and VPC/on-prem deployment constraints. Agreed next steps: run Redwood's quantization eval on customer's prompt set, schedule in-person bench run, share quantization results spreadsheet and security docs.
topics: INT8 vs FP8 vs GPTQ vs AWQ
KV cache and prefix caching behavior
action_items: Samir Patel - Share quantization evaluation spreadsheet + AWQ/GPTQ comparison (due 2026-10-25)
Tom Becker - Provide representative prompt set + traffic profile (due 2026-10-23)
Priya Nair - Schedule bench run on Dedicated pool (due 2026-10-29)
Olga Petrov - Confirm required compliance docs (SOC2 scope, KMS requirements) (due 2026-10-26)
next_steps: Redwood to run GPTQ/AWQ/INT8 experiments on Stargazer's prompt set and share accuracy/cost/latency sheet
Schedule 2-hour benchmark session on dedicated hardware with Stargazer's sample workload
Send Private/VPC deployment checklist and KMS integration guide
Follow-up call to review results and discuss rollout plan
transcript:
[00:00] Ian (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll run through the quantization tradeoffs and some of the perf numbers Samir has been running. quick agenda: accuracy, latency, kv cache, then deployment constraints.
[00:18] Maya (Stargazer): Thanks. we are mostly worried about regression on our safety-critical responses and also tail-latency for short chat interactions.
[00:28] Samir (Redwood SE): Yep understood. quick note up front: most of the numbers we'll discuss are on 8-bit GPTQ and also some AWQ and FP8 spots, these are approximate and we will run them on your prompt set.
[00:44] Tom (ML Eng): can you define AWQ vs GPTQ real fast? i've seen both used interchangably in slack threads but not sure of the exact trade-off.
[00:52] Samir: Sure — GPTQ is post-training quantization using per-channel grouping, tends to be conservative and retains accuracy but can be heavier to run; AWQ is more aggressive weight quant, often gives better compression and speed but sometimes larger accuracy variance, especially on long context.
[01:12] Lena (Redwood): and FP8 sits in between — it's lower bitwidth in float representation and often preserves distribution better than naive int8 but requires runtime/hardware support.
[01:25] Ravi (SRE): Our infra team prefers INT8 because it's broadly supported on our fleet, we don't have FP8 enabled everywhere.
[01:31] Priya (Redwood Product): right, that matters for Dedicated and on-prem: if your fleet is older GPUs we may be limited to INT8 or GPTQ variants.
[01:42] Olga (Security): also want to call out, for any on-prem or VPC deployment we need explicit KMS integration and audit logs, we'll review compliance later.
[01:50] Samir: ok jumping into numbers — baseline float32 throughput on 1xA100 is X tokens/sec, GPTQ-int8 variant gave about 2.8x token throughput, AWQ-int8 gave 3.2x in our internal bench but with a 1.5-3% drop on some reasoning benchmarks; FP8 on hardware that supports it gave 3.0x with much lower regression <1% on our eval set.
[02:18] Tom: that 1.5-3% drop, what metrics are you measuring? perplexity? instruction-following score?
[02:25] Samir: good q — it's a mix: instr-follow accuracy, BLEU-style in some tasks, and a custom safety/regression suite (we saw more diffs on multi-step reasoning). we'll quantify on your prompts.
[02:38] Maya: multi-step reasoning is a big one for us — we saw small hallucinations on a 6-7 step query when we tried an early AWQ run internally.
[02:46] Samir: that's consistent; AWQ sometimes perturbs weights that affect iterative attention. mitigation strategies: small calibration datasets for GPTQ, using mixed precision for critical layers, or keeping KV cache in FP16 while weights are int8.
[03:06] Tom: can you explain 'keeping KV cache in FP16' — does that mean the cache is separate from the quantized weights?
[03:12] Lena: yes — weights are quantized for matmul, but the KV cache stores activations/keys in fp16 which preserves numerical stability across long contexts. that reduces accuracy regressions at the cost of a bit more memory.
[03:26] Ravi: memory isn't our main constraint but latency for short chats (avg 120 tokens) is. how does batching interact here?
[03:33] Samir: batching helps throughput but hurts p99 latency. we recommend dynamic batching with small time window (e.g., 10ms) for short chat; combined with prefix KV caching that caches common system prompts you can get both latency and cost benefits.
[03:48] Tom: does the KV cache survive across requests for different sessions? can't leak between users?
[03:53] Ian: security-first: per-tenant isolation — the cache is namespaced per customer/session, we never reuse across tenants. for private deployments you'll control the storage; for hosted we provide strong tenant isolation and audit logs.
[04:06] Olga: want that in writing. our SOC2 scope needs to see cache life-cycle and deletion policies.
[04:12] Priya: we'll send the security checklist and KMS docs after — included in next steps.
[04:18] Samir: about latency numbers — for INT8 GPTQ on our dedicated hardware with dynamic batching we see median latency for 128-token responses around 45-55ms per token, p95 around 210-260ms depending on load; AWQ variants lower med latency by 10-15% but p95 can be worse if a regression triggers fallback.
[04:45] Tom: you mentioned fallback — what's the rollback/automatic fallback behavior?
[04:49] Samir: Redwood runtime supports automatic fallback policies: if quality or latency SLOs are missed, traffic can be routed to a less-quantized/FP16 variant. that adds complexity but keeps SLAs.
[04:59] Maya: how expensive is the fallback in terms of cost?
[05:03] Priya: cost delta depends on the model and infra; roughly 2-3x token cost when falling back to FP16 or float32 for the same model. we'll show exact numbers for your model in the spreadsheet.
[05:12] Tom: any special considerations for on-prem GPUs? we have a mixed fleet: some T4s, some A10s and a couple of H100s in the DR site.
[05:21] Samir: H100s can support FP8 and give great perf; T4s are limited to int8 paths and may not support some AWQ kernels. our recommendation: use H100 pool for latency-sensitive endpoints and T4/A10 for lower-cost batch endpoints; Redwood can route by policy.
[05:38] Ravi: we plan a VPC deployment first; question about KV eviction and disk persistence — can the cache be checkpointed if instance restarts?
[05:48] Lena: we support both in-memory and optional encrypted disk-backed cache. for on-prem you can configure persistence to your encrypted NFS, and keys are wrapped with your KMS.
[05:57] Olga: encryption at rest and in transit, plus KMS key rotation — we'll need the KMS integration guide.
[06:03] Ian: noted — action item.
[06:06] Samir: we should talk about the accuracy regression debug flow — we run delta tests on your prompt set and instrument layer-wise errors, then try mixed-precision or calibration removals on specific attention/ffn layers. sometimes a single layer in AWQ causes the majority of the delta.
[06:23] Tom: interesting — so we could do hybrid quantization? like keep some layers in fp16?
[06:27] Samir: exactly — hybrid configs are common: quantize the bulk but keep a handful of sensitive layers at higher precision. it's a common way to get most of the perf wins with minimal accuracy loss.
[06:39] Maya: what's the expected time to run your experiments on our 2k prompt set?
[06:44] Samir: assuming perf profiling + accuracy run, about 48 hours if we have access to your sample workload and a dedicated bench slot; quicker if you provide typical traffic traces.
[06:53] Priya: we'll schedule the bench run once Tom shares the prompt set.
[06:57] Tom: I'll upload dataset today.
[07:00] Lena: last topic — telemetry and rollouts: Redwood has per-route dashboards, regression alerts when eval metrics cross thresholds, and can automate canary rollouts with gradual traffic shifts.
[07:11] Ravi: good, we need that for ops.
[07:14] Maya: ok recap?
[07:16] Ian: recap — Redwood to run quantization experiments (GPTQ/AWQ/INT8/FP8 where supported) on your prompt set, share spreadsheet with accuracy/latency/cost; schedule dedicated bench run; send security/KMS docs. Samir will lead the experiments, Priya will schedule.
[07:31] Olga: thanks everyone.
[07:34] Ian: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the spreadsheet.
[07:38] [END]
